Write approximately 120 words in one paragraph without bullet points. Use English.
output_text: Binary search is an efficient algorithm for finding an item in a **sorted** array by repeatedly dividing the search interval in half. It starts with two pointers, one at the beginning (left) and one at the end (right) of the array. The algorithm compares the target value to the middle element (mid) of the current interval; if they match, the search succeeds. If the target is smaller, the search continues in the left half, otherwise, it proceeds to the right half. This process repeats, narrowing the interval until the target is found or the interval is empty. Binary search requires the input array to be **sorted** and supports **comparable elements**, typically integers or strings. Its time complexity is **O(log n)**, making it significantly faster than linear search for large datasets.
